explanation: Softmax, LayerNorm and batch-1 decode do a handful of FLOPs per byte, far below the ridge point of 333, so bandwidth bounds them. The big matmul does about 2,700 FLOPs per byte. Flash attention never writes the `N × N` score matrix to HBM, so its intensity grows with sequence length, and at 8K it is compute-bound; the original unfused attention, which writes the scores out, is memory-bound. PCIe only matters for host-device copies, which none of these kernels do.
